decisions.finding: MacRumors and 9to5Mac independently establish the initial iOS 9 public-beta appearance on 2015-07-09. The explicitly numbered Public Beta 2 coverage on 2015-07-22 establishes the launch appearance as sequence 1.
decisions.requiredQualification: Public Beta 1 is a normalized site label, not a claim that Apple or both launch reports displayed that literal ordinal. The retained 9to5Mac URL slug also ends in ios-9-public-beta-2 despite its headline and body describing the initial public launch.

decisions.finding: MacRumors and 9to5Mac independently and explicitly identify iOS 9 Public Beta 2 on 2015-07-22.
MacRumors and 9to5Mac independently identify the third iOS 9 public-beta appearance on 2015-08-06.
MacRumors establishes the initial iOS 10 public-beta availability and 9to5Mac explicitly identifies Public Beta 1 on 2016-07-07.
MacRumors and 9to5Mac independently and explicitly identify iOS 10 Public Beta 2 on 2016-07-20.
MacRumors and 9to5Mac independently and explicitly identify iOS 10 Public Beta 3 on 2016-08-02.

iDevice.ro explicitly reports Public Beta 4 on 2016-08-09, MacRumors records same-day public-tester availability, and CHIP independently says the fourth public beta had been available since Tuesday evening.
decisions.requiredQualification: Use the article headline, body, and publication metadata rather than the misleading iDevice.ro URL slug ending in ios-10-public-beta-5. CHIP's next-day publication corroborates the August 9 appearance through its Tuesday-evening wording.

decisions.finding: 9to5Mac and TechCrunch independently and explicitly identify iOS 10 Public Beta 5 on 2016-08-15.
9to5Mac and TechCrunch independently and explicitly identify iOS 10 Public Beta 6 on 2016-08-19.
MacRumors and 9to5Mac independently and explicitly identify iOS 10 Public Beta 7 on 2016-08-26.

qualifications.subject: iOS 9.0 Public Beta 1 display label and source metadata
qualifications.finding: The chronology and normalized sequence are well supported, but the literal Public Beta 1 label is not consistently displayed in the launch reports. The two launch sources are therefore appearance evidence, not literal-ordinal evidence.
qualifications.requiredHandling: Preserve ordinalBasis=normalizedFirstAppearance and the candidate qualification. Do not claim Apple displayed the exact Public Beta 1 label on 2015-07-09.

qualifications.subject: iOS 10.0 Public Beta 4 publisher artifacts
qualifications.finding: The retained iDevice.ro URL slug says Public Beta 5 although its headline and body repeatedly say Public Beta 4; CHIP published the following day while describing availability since Tuesday evening.
qualifications.requiredHandling: Preserve the existing qualification and cite article content and timestamps, not the misleading slug.

qualifications.subject: production reconciliation wording
qualifications.finding: The preserved query counts all publicBeta events within the two scoped release versions rather than issuing ten separate exact-identity queries. Because that scoped count is zero, it still proves every candidate exact match is zero. A fresh read-only rerun produced the same result.
qualifications.requiredHandling: Repeat the scoped or exact identity query immediately before any separately authorized write.

authorization.chronologyApprovalScope: Public-beta appearance identity, date, sequence, channel, and paired developer route only; qualifications remain mandatory.
